Name: Michael Lee
Details:
Dec 1, 2024 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. faffed around the bottom trying to get up onto the rail before figuring out the move - using a slightly raised bump for RH, then placing LF at the low obvious undercling and raising RF, before going LH scumming up the rail until a really good slot. Bring heel up, bump RH into an intermediate gaston (or skip it) before bringing RH around a small hump, then finally to the arete. you can use the arete and step up a little LF to clip the second bolt - just be careful here not to slip. climb up and right staying near the arete before clipping third bolt, and take a long rest. Then, move left across the face, using a low RH crimp to control yourself as you lean left and get LH into a jug. sort both hands properly on the jug, get LF high onto an obvious rail, and lean back into the jug LH. probably clip from here, then use a RH rail to crimp and bring the thumb over, before sorting feet and LF onto the jug. LH up to an unlikely triangle pinch about a foot above the 4th bolt, bring hips around onto a right face, squeeze RF in and scum up before throwing RH to a great flat/sticky hold. use a couple feet on a chunk of rock that moves down and towards the right arete for feet to grab around the side and get a good visual, before making a somewhat committing move over to the arete. from here, it's just a trivial step up and a jug to the anchors.

Overall, when I went to set up the route, I faffed at the first bolt trying to figure out the beta (don't use the chalked sidepull, etc.), then went all the way up until the upper crux. was kinda heady without knowing the beta, and I ended up using a LH pinch that felt solid enough if you pulled further back, but jiggled enough to warrant some safety concern. clipped the fourth bolt, and then faffed around again trying to figure out the route to the anchors. tried going left, tried going right, tried left again, then eventually pulled around the arete.

A great route for which good beta in one or two places is the key di…

Name: Michael Lee
Details: Nov 16, 2024 ·  Lead / Flash. Didn’t talk too much beta, but got a little nonetheless. Alex placed the draws, I led and cleaned on the lower (not ideal but not so bad). Pretty varied with a couple of committing, but safe, moves. The first two bolts are pretty easy, the 3rd a little less so but still fairly easy. Find a heel around the left arete to clip the 4th, then use some high feet and reachy, committing moves to get to a good ledge. Stay mid-high with LF on the ledge (there are two levels, press out and left w/ LF just below the second level of the ledge) and get RF over to a small lip. Use the sidepulls to make a balance-y and slightly reachy move before matching and getting RF out again. Trust some slightly marginal feet and find the few decent handholds before topping out onto a really dirty ledge at the anchor. Overall, varied climbing on fairly decent rock, with good protection, good length, and an easy location right at the north trail loop makes this one of the most worthwhile routes at the gorge.

Details: Nov 9, 2024 ·  Lead. Finally sent, with first draw pre-clipped. Still not really sure about the beta before the block-y obvious hold, but once you get there and clip the second draw (kinda scary still), you can use the dish above the second hold as a LF, and the right side of the block as a RF before reaching up into the RH divot and going for the LH gaston. Pushed RF into the huge LH sidepull that’s near bolt #2, matched feet, then RF high to rock over and press RH out straight right before leaning just a bit more and grabbing the sidepull. Match feet/get both feet over right before LH high and clipping 3rd draw. Bit heady, as a fall here requires an attentive belay. From after the 3rd clip, it’s all easy stuff as it links up with dwarrowdelf - the moves can’t be more than 5.5 or so.

Details: Mar 9, 2024 ·  Lead. I struggled to figure out where the route starts. Here’s what I think it is: to the right of the ramp there’s a giant rock formation that comes forward away from the rest of the route. To the very left front facing of that rock are a set of “steps” . They’re not generous but that’s all ya got. Really no good place to put pro to protect this part. I put a small cam in a crack to the right . But I’m sure it wasn’t doing much. Anyways, go up the steps to the top of the rock. The top is gritty and grippy . If you just keep taking the steps you will be ok to pull yourself up the top due to nice rough rock. Walk back to the wall. Head up left to follow the line to a single bolt a little bit before the anchor. Use the bolt. There’s no place to put gear at the top and some angel sent to earth put that bolt there for us. Thank you climbing angel who did that. Scariest 5.2 of my life (because of leading )

Details: Feb 19, 2023 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Flake into left Gaston. match on two rails and then high left foot. right foot up into side of start holds and pull into solid underling. left hand out to sloper and right up to triangle. left foot on the chalked up divet and high left right foot up. step up with the right foot into a Gaston. then transfer into sloper. match on sloper and get a higher left foot. pull into great ledge.scramble up into crack. layback in crack on right foot. high right foot pulls into underling and then to a rail. small right foot below rail reaches to massive horn. finish.

Name: Michael Lee
Details: Feb 19, 2023 ·  TR. At the bottom I just put RF up very high and took the higher decent LH crimp in the seam. LF into the small corner, just find whatever works and step up hard into RH undercling. Fix feet and LH into sloper. Get RF over farther right on the rail and reach into triangle pinch. Match feet and RF up (others liked the small slightly slopey foothold below the large rail, but i still preferred the larger rail with RF, make sure to maximize surface area with RF), then bring LH into a sidepull above RH. Rock over hard onto RF and get the small incut crimps. Sort feet and layback with LH reach up into the sloper. Match, then get into jug system. Get to last bolt and do a layback with back facing left. Find a nice inner rail in the crack. Base of the crack is good LF and then step up high into RF. Good rail about face height once over RF and then some decent smaller stuff to the left. Use those and get to a huge horn jug LH.

Name: Michael Lee
Details: Feb 19, 2023 ·  Lead. Set up today. Little slow at the bottom, forgot to bump up with RF.

Name: Michael Lee
Details: Feb 19, 2023 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. At bottom step farther left to get higher on the large rail, then get right foot below the obvious foothold in the middle. Right hand crimp is pretty positive, use the middle seams with LH and get up LF. Then right hand to the block, and RH high and rest. Feet here are very marginal. LH match the blocky piece, then step onto RF and reach up RH gaston. Clip with LH, then go just above and left of RH gaston to undercling LH, and step LF into a divot near the block. Pull in with the LH undercling and go up and slightly left into RH pinch. Get to the good LH gaston, RF into the gaston to the right of the 2nd bolt. RH match, LF into the dish, put RF up a little to a good hold and rock over into obvious RH gaston. Get RH around the gaston block into a sidepull, then push straight up into a very good RH ledge above the sidepull. Clip with LH, pull right into the clear.

Name: Michael Lee
Details:
Mar 14, 2022 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Faffed about quite a bit. Getting to the first bolt requires a kind of crappy foot for me and using the crimp down and right from the block. A bit of a move up with the right hand to a gaston allows for a secure clipping position when you find your feet. Left hand undercling and find some bad feet to secure a right hand pinch, then go right foot pressing out and left foot to a kind of circle. Left hand up and far left to a small sharp jug, and match right hand. Get right foot high, Push over into a right hand gaston, grab around the gaston with right for a side pull to help secure, and do what you need to get your left up, rotate your left to face left, and then eventually stand up and clip. Careful - gets a bit heady here, and a loose belay could lead to a ground fall. I almost hit the ground too - belayer can find a comfortable stance climbers left of the route that will help to reduce amount of rope out, but it will lead to a little bit of a swing, so watch out for that. Above the third bolt there’s no protection, but the climbing goes much easier, maybe around 5.5. So be careful and don’t whip cause… I’m not sure what’d happen to you then. 

Bad climbing today meant a big whip all the way to the bottom and also a medium size fall later when I tried from the ground up again. Both big falls were on the gaston move, where the feet are awkward and the position is scrunched. Eventually made it, but it was a bit heady and my mentality wasn’t amazing today. Ended up climbing up to the second bolt, resting, and then doing that section and finishing. Rather disappointing, but at least made it in the end..

Name: Michael Lee
Details:
Jan 30, 2022 ·  Lead / Flash. At the base, you can clip the first bolt basically standing if you’re even 5’8”ish. I had to step up a bit and then started. Find a good left foot plate to stand up on, before using the obvious large right flake. Great RH undercling and a left hand let you get the second clip, though I forgot here and had to move past. Get the sorta bad left hand sloper sorted, then stand up right and reach a bit for the triangle-ly pinch. You’ll have to match feet and hands before getting your right hand to a sorta cruddy pinch and right foot out to the side - I used the big pad of my foot and didn’t need a heel (maybe it would’ve been better? Maybe I would’ve been lower so it would’ve been worse? Not sure.?) and stepped up enough to get my left hand up and right. This big chalked part has a decent lower part, which you can use to get comfy before getting to the even better higher part. You can quick rest, or get feet up left a little and reach to a great LH ledge. This gives you a great chance to get a right hand clip at your waist. Then, rest a bit, and use two great slots in the crack to layback a couple moves and get your hands up. Find some acceptable but not great feet, then there’s a big rail that’s decent for your left hand. Get this with a right hand slightly low and in the crack, and bump the left hand enough over that you can get the best part of the rail with your right hand. Pull hard, and get your left hand over the slope to a flattish area. You’ll get high enough to see a big triangular jug - but on the flattish area, about 1/3 from the ledge to the jug, is a good enough rail crimp that you can get solid on, before getting to the glorious jug and top out. Just use a bit of caution to walk right on a thin line to place your anchor.
Super fun and quite pumpy for the right arm. One of my favorite leads - maybe my favorite.

Name: Michael Lee
Details:
Jan 30, 2022 ·  Lead / Flash. Start near top of the pseudo staircase, clip around the corner with a strong left side pull, then get onto the ledge with both hands, locking off, finding a high-ish right foot plate, then moving right hand up to another ledge -> then a bump slightly more right and deeper to grab a great plate. Move your left hand over, stand up,
And you’re out of the crux. When you get to the huge chalked pinch, grab it right hand thumb left, then left hand a touch higher with thumb right. Get your feet sorted then push out left and up to a slightly reachy right hand jug. From here, much easier climbing to get to two close bolts for a QuickDraw anchor.
Belayer should stand at the level the climber is, and when the climber gets to a good place, the belayer can move down a couple steps for a better position.

Name: Michael Lee
Details: Dec 5, 2021 ·  Lead / Onsight. Had Aaron place the first draw and clip it, from worrying about 1) decking or 2) decking, then tumbling off. That being said, if you’re strong enough and get a good grip on the first okay holds, then you can stand up on the first hold and place the first draw and clip it. A bit of a tricky move above the first clip, then move a little to the arete. Second bolt is also accessible from a stable position. You’ll have to move right again to get to the 3rd bolt - don’t get too drawn left or you’ll leave the bolt line. You get above the second bolt and get another tricky move - perhaps the last - and then have to climb easier, but not trivial, terrain that requires some balance and a little searching (you can find okay holds if you look with care). You’ll get to some easy stuff and be able to clip the third bolt, then you’re pretty run out to the 4th bolt - if you fall just before it’s a huge whip and you might need your belayer to run backwards to keep you from decking... not sure if I’m exaggerating frankly. You can place pro in the horizontal crack (maybe a tricam would be great here honestly…) but a huge rail and some great feet bring you onto a ledge without too much trouble. You can move a little more right and get the bolt, and go up to the anchors, or stay left where it might be marginally easier, and go all the way. Fun route and good lead!

Details:
Oct 3, 2021 ·  TR. The approach to the base of the climb was relatively straightforward. The Trauma is on the north side of Lunch Rock. Look for the distinctive dihedral near the top. 

We only brought gear for top roping so I had to make the VERY sketchy scramble up to the anchors. It took me about 45 minutes b/c I had no idea where I was going; could probably make it to the anchor bolts in 15-20 mins next time. 

The scramble starts just south of Lunch Rock; there’s a (low 5th class?) scramble up through a brush-filled depression in the gorge wall. It should be fairly obvious. 

Once you’re past the scramble, keep hiking up the trail until you’re north of lunch rock (I used the power lines across the gorge as a landmark). I believe I passed two other trails that went left. I took the third (?) trail which went straight down towards the face. It eventually worked its way back to the south towards Lunch Rock. Closer to the anchor is a bit of a scramble.

The anchors were on a small clearing at the top of Lunch Rock. There should be 3 or 4 sets of bolts near each other.
